observations: The first 31c batch is event-heavy: three event-flow packets and seven actor event-condition packets.
SetTalk/SetNotice/SetEmote share the 0x38 game-message-body envelope with small selectors followed by fixed ASCII condition-name slots.
SetPushCircle, SetPushFan, and SetPushBox carry packed flag bytes; bit 4 is the outwards or inverted-bound test flag, while fan and box keep their own bit-0 conventions.
SetEventStatus remains a useful alignment trap: enabled is a u32, not a u8, and conditionType is at payload+4.

observations: Batch 2 processes ten receiver-map rows but emits nine payloadStructs because 0x0133 UserDataReceiver is duplicated in the map.
Most player-state packets in this batch are standard 0x28 or 0x30 packet envelopes where the client applies only a low byte or low dword and leaves reserved padding.
0x0133 GenericData is a 0xc0-byte LuaParam stream in the server-to-client direction; the same numeric opcode has a separate client-to-server GroupCreated meaning.
0x01a5 carries the item-storage bitstream: receiver-map evidence documents 32 supported bytes

observations: Batch 3 finishes the currently mapped-but-unbound receiver list: 8 receiver rows and 8 payloadStructs.
SendLog-family packets split into an actor1 tier (0x0157, 0x10-byte payload) and the no-source text-sheet x28 tier (0x0166, 8-byte payload).

0x0166 has competing receiver-map evidence: captures/opcodes classify it as SendLog/TextSheetNoSource, while a SetCommandEventConditionReceiver row also maps the same 8-byte body. Both variants are preserved.
SyncMemory 0x0137 is a variable property stream with a leading running-length byte and dynamic type-tagged records.
HamletSupplyRanking and HamletDefenseScore are content-gated and unobserved; their total sizes are marked decomp-inferred from helper iteration/allocation widths.
